tagline: Capital of rickshaws, Mughal lanes and river ports
intro: Bangladesh's capital and largest city, spread along the Buriganga and Turag rivers. Old Dhaka holds the Mughal and colonial layers; newer districts hold museums, universities and the country's busiest food scene.
transport: Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport; intercity trains from Kamalapur; long-distance buses from Sayedabad, Gabtoli and Mohakhali.

highlights.name: Ahsan Manzil
highlights.note: Restored 19th-century nawab palace on the Buriganga, now a museum.

highlights.name: Lalbagh Fort
highlights.note: Unfinished Mughal fort complex with the tomb of Pari Bibi.

highlights.name: Star Mosque
highlights.note: 18th-century mosque decorated with blue-star mosaic tiles.

highlights.name: National Museum
highlights.note: Ethnography, archaeology and art collections in Shahbagh.

intro: A riverine district on the south bank of the Padma, known for jute history, boat traffic and the new Padma Bridge approach at Bhanga.
transport: Buses from Dhaka via the Padma Bridge (about 2.5 hours); rail link to Bhanga.

highlights.name: Padma River ghat
highlights.note: Working river port with country boats and ferries at sunset.

highlights.name: Bhanga Padma Bridge view
highlights.note: The southern approach to the Padma Bridge, a popular drive.

intro: A rapidly industrialising district north of Dhaka that still holds substantial sal forest and a safari park at Dulalpur.
transport: Buses and commuter trains from Dhaka; about 1–2 hours depending on traffic.

highlights.name: Bhawal National Park
highlights.note: Sal forest and grassland, best walked in the cool season.

highlights.name: Bangabandhu Safari Park
highlights.note: Large drive-through wildlife park at Dulalpur.

highlights.name: Nuhash Polli
highlights.note: Humayun Ahmed's rural retreat, open to visitors.

tagline: Haors, rivers and the birthplace of Bangabandhu
intro: A low-lying district of rivers and wetlands in south-central Bangladesh, home to the Bangabandhu Memorial Museum at Tungipara.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 4 hours); rail via Rajbari.

highlights.name: Bangabandhu Memorial Museum, Tungipara
highlights.note: Birthplace complex and mausoleum, a national memorial site.

highlights.name: Madhumati River
highlights.note: Wide river runs along the district's western edge.

intro: A district of haors and rivers north-east of Dhaka, known for the Pagla Mosque, Shah Mahmud Mosque and the Nikli haor wetland.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 3 hours); rail to Kishoreganj town.

highlights.name: Pagla Mosque
highlights.note: Ornate mosque and shrine complex in Kishoreganj town.

highlights.name: Shah Mahmud Mosque
highlights.note: Mughal-era mosque with fine terracotta decoration.

highlights.name: Nikli Haor
highlights.note: Seasonal wetland best seen by boat in the monsoon and after.

intro: A small riverine district between the Padma and the Arial Khan, with a rural landscape of jute fields and ferry crossings.
transport: Buses from Dhaka via the Padma Bridge; launch services on the Padma.

highlights.name: Shakuni Dighi
highlights.note: Historic tank and lakeside area used for local walks.

highlights.name: Padma riverbank
highlights.note: Ferry ghats and fishing boats along the district's northern edge.

intro: A district west of Dhaka whose riverbank villages hold some of the best-preserved zamindar houses in central Bangladesh.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 2 hours); the Padma Bridge improves access to the south.

highlights.name: Baliati Zamindar Bari
highlights.note: Large 19th-century mansion with a courtyard and temple.

highlights.name: Teota Zamindar Bari
highlights.note: Riverside palace ruins with carved facades.

intro: A delta district just south of Dhaka, historically part of Bikrampur and dotted with archaeological sites and riverside forts.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 1.5 hours); launches on the Dhaleshwari.

highlights.name: Idrakpur Fort
highlights.note: Mughal river fort built to defend the old water route.

highlights.name: Bikrampur archaeological sites
highlights.note: Scattered Buddhist and Hindu remains around Rampal and Bajrayogini.

intro: The old river port and jute trading town beside Dhaka, and the centre of Bangladesh's jamdani weaving tradition.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 1 hour); launches from Sadarghat.

highlights.name: Sonargaon Panam City
highlights.note: Abandoned merchant street of colonial-era houses.

highlights.name: Folk Arts and Crafts Museum
highlights.note: Sonargaon museum of Bengali craft and folk art.

highlights.name: Rupganj jamdani workshops
highlights.note: Working handloom villages where jamdani is woven.

intro: A district north-east of Dhaka with one of the most important early historic archaeological sites in Bangladesh.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 2 hours); rail to Narsingdi.

highlights.name: Wari-Bateshwar
highlights.note: Early historic settlement site with evidence of trade with the wider region.

highlights.name: Meghna riverbank
highlights.note: Wide river views and boat traffic.

intro: A small district at the Padma crossing, historically important as the Goalanda river port and rail terminus.
transport: Trains from Dhaka to Goalanda; buses via the Padma Bridge.

highlights.name: Goalanda Ghat
highlights.note: Historic ferry and rail terminus on the Padma.

highlights.name: Rajbari Zamindar Bari
highlights.note: District-town palace associated with the local rajas.

intro: A delta district on the Padma's south bank, made up largely of char land shaped and reshaped by the river.
transport: Buses from Dhaka via Padma Bridge (about 3 hours).

highlights.name: Padma char land
highlights.note: Farming islands and ferry crossings in the main channel.

intro: North-west of Dhaka, Tangail is known for its handloom sarees, the Madhupur sal forest and the Atia Mosque.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 2.5 hours); rail to Tangail.

highlights.name: Atia Mosque
highlights.note: Early 17th-century mosque with terracotta ornament.

highlights.name: Mohera Zamindar Bari
highlights.note: Restored zamindar complex with a temple and gardens.

highlights.name: Madhupur Forest
highlights.note: Sal forest and Garo villages on the Tangail–Mymensingh border.

intro: The most mountainous district in the country, home to Marma, Mro and Tripura communities and peaks above 1,000 metres.
transport: Buses from Chattogram (about 3 hours) and Dhaka (overnight). Some areas need permits.

highlights.name: Nilgiri
highlights.note: Hill viewpoint and resort area with wide ridge views.

highlights.name: Boga Lake
highlights.note: Hill lake near Ruma, reached by road and trail.

highlights.name: Chimbuk Hill
highlights.note: Drive-up ridge with layered hill views.

highlights.name: Keokradong
highlights.note: One of the country's highest peaks, a demanding guided trek.

intro: A district of rivers and fertile plains on the route east to Sylhet, historically a centre of classical music.
transport: Trains and buses from Dhaka (about 3 hours).

highlights.name: Ashuganj river port
highlights.note: Major river port on the Meghna with boat traffic and ghats.

highlights.name: Meghna–Titas riverbank
highlights.note: Fishing villages and seasonal wetlands.

tagline: Hilsa capital at the river confluence
intro: Where the Padma and Meghna meet, Chandpur is famous for hilsa and its working river port.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 3 hours); launches from Sadarghat.

highlights.name: Padma–Meghna confluence
highlights.note: Wide meeting of rivers, best seen from the town ghats.

highlights.name: Chandpur fish market
highlights.note: Early-morning hilsa auction at the river port.

tagline: Port city between hills and sea
intro: Bangladesh's second city and main port, set between the Bay of Bengal and the hill tracts, with beaches, museums and a war cemetery.
transport: Airport; intercity trains from Dhaka; buses from all major cities.

highlights.name: Patenga Beach
highlights.note: City beach where the Karnaphuli meets the sea.

highlights.name: Commonwealth War Cemetery
highlights.note: Immaculately kept WWII cemetery for Allied and local personnel.

highlights.name: Ethnological Museum
highlights.note: Collections on the region's indigenous communities.

highlights.name: Foy's Lake
highlights.note: Lakeside park and amusement area.

intro: An old district on the road to Chattogram, home to the Mainamati archaeological area and a distinctive rasmalai tradition.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 2.5 hours); rail to Cumilla.

highlights.name: Mainamati
highlights.note: Cluster of Buddhist viharas and stupas from the 7th–12th centuries.

highlights.name: Cumilla War Cemetery
highlights.note: Commonwealth cemetery for WWII casualties.

highlights.name: BARD
highlights.note: Rural development academy campus and demonstration village.

intro: Bangladesh's tourism capital, with a 120 km beach, hill-and-sea viewpoints, and the boat route to Saint Martin's Island.
transport: Flights from Dhaka (about 1 hour); overnight buses (9–11 hours).

highlights.name: Himchari National Park
highlights.note: Hills falling to the sea, waterfalls in the monsoon.

highlights.name: Inani Beach
highlights.note: Quieter coral-stone beach south of the main town.

highlights.name: Teknaf and the Naf River
highlights.note: Southern tip of mainland Bangladesh.

intro: A small, busy district on the road and rail line between Dhaka and Chattogram, close to the Indian border.
transport: Trains and buses from Dhaka and Chattogram.

highlights.name: Muhuri River
highlights.note: Border river with ghats and small boat traffic.

highlights.name: Feni river embankment
highlights.note: Rural walks and seasonal wetlands.

intro: A hill district of forests and Tripura communities, with caves, waterfalls and the road north to Sajek.
transport: Buses from Chattogram (about 3 hours) and Dhaka (overnight).

highlights.name: Alutila Cave
highlights.note: Narrow cave passage visited with a local guide.

highlights.name: Richhang Waterfall
highlights.note: Seasonal waterfall in the hills outside town.

highlights.name: Chengi River
highlights.note: Clear river running through the district.

intro: A low delta district on the Meghna, reached by road from Dhaka and by river from the south.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 4 hours); launches on the Meghna.

highlights.name: Meghna riverbank
highlights.note: Fishing villages and ferry ghats along the estuary.

highlights.name: Dalal Bazar
highlights.note: Historic river-trade market.

intro: A coastal district in the Meghna estuary, including the offshore chars and Nijhum Dwip wildlife area.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 4–5 hours) and Chattogram.

highlights.name: Nijhum Dwip
highlights.note: Mangrove island and wildlife sanctuary in the estuary.

highlights.name: Meghna estuary char land
highlights.note: Seasonal islands reached by boat.

intro: A hill district built around Kaptai Lake, with Chakma and Marma communities and boat routes to island markets.
transport: Buses from Chattogram (about 3 hours) and Dhaka (overnight).

highlights.name: Kaptai Lake
highlights.note: Reservoir with forested islands and boat markets.

highlights.name: Jhulonto Bridge
highlights.note: Suspension footbridge over the lake.

highlights.name: Shuvolong Waterfall
highlights.note: Waterfall reached by boat, strongest after the monsoon.

highlights.name: Rajban Bihar
highlights.note: Buddhist monastery and meditation centre.

intro: A north-central district holding Mahasthangarh, the oldest known urban site in Bangladesh, and famous for sweet yoghurt.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 5 hours); rail to Bogura.

highlights.name: Mahasthangarh
highlights.note: Fortified early historic city with museum and ruins.

highlights.name: Behular Bashor Ghor
highlights.note: Monument linked to the Behula–Lakhindar legend.

highlights.name: Gokul Medh
highlights.note: Excavated mound with terraced brick structure.

intro: Bangladesh's mango heartland on the Padma, with some of the country's finest Sultanate-era brick mosques.
best: May–July for mangoes; November–February for sites
transport: Buses from Rajshahi (about 2 hours) and Dhaka (overnight).

highlights.name: Choto Sona Masjid
highlights.note: Finely carved 15th-century stone mosque.

highlights.name: Darashbari Mosque
highlights.note: Large Sultanate mosque with a domed prayer hall.

highlights.name: Mango orchards
highlights.note: Orchard visits and roadside mango markets in season.

intro: A small agricultural district in the north-west, with mango orchards, rice plains and lesser-visited archaeological remains.
transport: Trains and buses from Dhaka via Bogura.

highlights.name: Mango orchards
highlights.note: Summer orchards and local markets.

highlights.name: Rural river ghats
highlights.note: Small rivers and seasonal wetlands across the district.

intro: A district in the Barind tract holding Paharpur's UNESCO-listed Buddhist monastery and the Kusumba Mosque.
transport: Buses from Rajshahi (about 3 hours) and Bogura.

highlights.name: Somapura Mahavihara, Paharpur
highlights.note: UNESCO World Heritage Buddhist monastery complex.

highlights.name: Kusumba Mosque
highlights.note: Black-stone mosque from the late Sultanate period.

intro: A district of old landed estates and wetland, with the Uttara Ganabhaban and the edge of the Chalan Beel.
transport: Buses and trains from Dhaka via Rajshahi.

highlights.name: Uttara Ganabhaban
highlights.note: Presidential retreat in a former zamindar palace.

highlights.name: Natore Rajbari
highlights.note: Colonnaded palace and temple complex.

highlights.name: Chalan Beel
highlights.note: Vast seasonal wetland, best in the monsoon.

intro: A district on the north bank of the Padma, known for the Hardinge Bridge, dairy sweets and river landscapes.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 3 hours); rail to Pabna.

highlights.name: Hardinge Bridge
highlights.note: Colonial-era railway bridge across the Padma, still standing.

highlights.name: Lalon Shah Bridge
highlights.note: Long road bridge over the Padma.

highlights.name: Chalan Beel
highlights.note: Wetland edges reach the district's north.

intro: A clean, manageable city on the Padma known for silk, mangoes, the Varendra Research Museum and its university campus.
transport: Airport; trains and buses from Dhaka (about 5 hours).

highlights.name: Varendra Research Museum
highlights.note: One of the oldest museums in the region, strong on regional archaeology.

highlights.name: Padma riverfront
highlights.note: Wide river views and evening walks.

highlights.name: Shah Makhdum Mosque
highlights.note: Old mosque and shrine in the city.

intro: A district on the Jamuna, dominated by the Jamuna Multipurpose Bridge and the river economy around it.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 3 hours); rail to Sirajganj.

highlights.name: Jamuna Bridge
highlights.note: Major road and rail crossing of the Jamuna.

highlights.name: Rabindra Kacharibari, Shahzadpur
highlights.note: Restored estate house associated with Rabindranath Tagore's family.

intro: A district holding the UNESCO-listed mosque city founded by Khan Jahan Ali, and the eastern gateway to the Sundarbans at Mongla.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 6 hours) and Khulna (about 1 hour).

highlights.name: Sixty Dome Mosque
highlights.note: UNESCO World Heritage Sultanate mosque.

highlights.name: Khan Jahan Ali Mausoleum
highlights.note: Shrine complex beside the Ghora Dighi tank.

highlights.name: Mongla Port
highlights.note: Departure point for Sundarbans boat trips.

intro: A small south-western district of riverside villages, known for its rural landscape and winter vegetables.
transport: Trains and buses from Dhaka via Jashore.

highlights.name: Mathabhanga River
highlights.note: River crossings and riverside farmland.

intro: A south-western district town known for flowers, the Benapole land port, and as a transport hub for the region.
transport: Airport; trains and buses from Dhaka (about 5 hours).

highlights.name: Godkhali flower market
highlights.note: One of the region's largest flower-growing areas, near Jhikargacha.

highlights.name: Sagardari Zamindar Bari
highlights.note: Riverside zamindar house with a temple.

highlights.name: Benapole land port
highlights.note: Main overland crossing to West Bengal.

intro: A district in the south-west with old landed estates, rural markets and riverine scenery.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 5 hours); rail to Jhenaidah.

highlights.name: Naldanga Rajbari
highlights.note: Zamindar palace complex with temples.

highlights.name: Gorai River
highlights.note: River ghats and fishing villages.

intro: The main city of the south-west and the usual departure point for Sundarbans trips, with a wide riverfront on the Rupsha.
transport: Airport; trains and buses from Dhaka (about 6–8 hours).

highlights.name: Rupsha Bridge
highlights.note: River crossing with launch terminals and fish markets.

highlights.name: Sundarbans departures
highlights.note: Boats leave from Khulna and Mongla for the reserve.

highlights.name: Khulna Divisional Museum
highlights.note: Regional history and archaeology collection.

intro: A district on the Padma associated with the Baul saint Lalon Shah and Rabindranath Tagore's Shilaidaha estate.
transport: Buses and trains from Dhaka (about 4–5 hours).

highlights.name: Lalon Shah's shrine
highlights.note: Akhrar and mausoleum of the Baul philosopher at Cheuria.

highlights.name: Shilaidaha Kuthibari
highlights.note: Tagore's riverside estate house, now a museum.

highlights.name: Hardinge Bridge
highlights.note: The bridge crosses the Padma near the district boundary.

intro: A small district in the south-west with river ghats, rice fields and a quiet rural pace.
transport: Buses from Dhaka via Jashore (about 5 hours).

highlights.name: Nabaganga River
highlights.note: River ghats and boat crossings.

intro: A small western district on the Indian border, historically significant as the site of the 1971 provisional government's oath ceremony.
transport: Buses from Dhaka via Kushtia (about 6 hours).

highlights.name: Mujibnagar Memorial
highlights.note: Memorial complex marking the 1971 provisional government.

intro: A district of small rivers and villages, known as the birthplace of painter SM Sultan.
transport: Buses from Dhaka via Jashore (about 5 hours).

highlights.name: Chitra River
highlights.note: Riverside walks and boat crossings in the district town.

highlights.name: SM Sultan's art school
highlights.note: The painter's home and school at Masimdia.

intro: The south-westernmost district, bordering the Indian Sundarbans, with shrimp farms, mangrove creeks and the Bhomra land port.
transport: Buses from Khulna (about 2 hours) and Dhaka (overnight).

highlights.name: Sundarbans Satkhira range
highlights.note: Mangrove creeks accessible with permits and a guide.

highlights.name: Bhomra land port
highlights.note: Border crossing to West Bengal.

intro: A coastal district at the mouth of the Bishkhali, with fishing communities and a long, little-visited shoreline.
transport: Buses from Barishal (about 3 hours) and Dhaka (overnight).

highlights.name: Patharghata beach
highlights.note: Coastal sand and fishing boat activity.

highlights.name: Bishkhali River
highlights.note: Wide river mouth with boat traffic.

intro: The hub of the southern delta, built on the Kirtankhola river, with launches to islands and a strong rice-and-fish food culture.
transport: Airport; launches from Dhaka (about 8 hours); buses via Padma Bridge.

highlights.name: Kirtankhola riverfront
highlights.note: Working ghats and evening river walks.

highlights.name: Durga Sagar
highlights.note: Large historic tank with a central island pavilion.

intro: Bangladesh's largest island district, formed by the Meghna estuary, with chars, beaches and the Monpura island.
transport: Launches from Dhaka and Barishal; buses after the Padma Bridge.

highlights.name: Char Kukri-Mukri
highlights.note: Mangrove and beach area on the Bay edge.

highlights.name: Monpura Island
highlights.note: Quiet island with wide mudflats and fishing life.

intro: A small delta district between the Sugandha and Bishkhali, famous for floating guava markets in winter.
transport: Buses from Barishal (about 40 minutes); launches from Dhaka.

highlights.name: Bhimruli floating guava market
highlights.note: Boats loaded with guavas at dawn during the winter harvest.

highlights.name: Sugandha River
highlights.note: Riverside town life and boat crossings.

intro: A coastal district home to Kuakata beach and Fatrar Char, the eastern approach to the Sundarbans.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 7 hours) and Barishal (about 3 hours).

highlights.name: Kuakata Beach
highlights.note: Beach with both sunrise and sunset over the sea.

highlights.name: Fatrar Char
highlights.note: Mangrove forest on the Sundarbans edge.

highlights.name: Payra Port
highlights.note: Deep-sea port area on the coast.

intro: A delta district of tidal rivers and orchards, with the floating guava market at Swarupkathi.
transport: Buses from Barishal (about 2 hours); launches from Dhaka.

highlights.name: Swarupkathi floating guava market
highlights.note: Seasonal boat market in the guava harvest.

highlights.name: Sandhya River
highlights.note: Tidal river with orchard banks.

intro: A district of tea estates, wetlands and the Satchhari National Park on the edge of the haor country.
transport: Trains and buses from Dhaka (about 4 hours).

highlights.name: Satchhari National Park
highlights.note: Small rainforest park with trails and wildlife.

highlights.name: Titas River
highlights.note: River ghats and rural wetlands.

intro: The tea heartland of Bangladesh, with Srimangal, Lawachara National Park and Madhabpur Lake.
transport: Trains from Dhaka to Srimangal (about 6 hours); buses.

highlights.name: Lawachara National Park
highlights.note: Rainforest trails and Hoolock gibbons.

highlights.name: Madhabpur Lake
highlights.note: Tea-estate lake with a small temple.

highlights.name: Finlay Tea Estate
highlights.note: Working estate with tea tastings.

intro: The heart of Bangladesh's haor wetlands, including Tanguar Haor, best explored by boat in winter.
transport: Buses from Sylhet (about 2.5 hours) and Dhaka (overnight).

highlights.name: Tanguar Haor
highlights.note: Ramsar wetland with winter birdlife and houseboats.

highlights.name: Jadukata River
highlights.note: Clear river along the Meghalaya foothills.

highlights.name: Niladri Lake
highlights.note: Blue-water lake formed in a former limestone quarry area.

intro: The north-east's main city, known for its Sufi shrines, tea gardens, and access to Jaflong, Ratargul and the haors.
transport: Airport; trains and buses from Dhaka (about 6–7 hours).

highlights.name: Hazrat Shah Jalal shrine
highlights.note: Major Sufi shrine in the old city.

highlights.name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
highlights.note: Freshwater swamp forest, flooded in the monsoon.

highlights.name: Jaflong
highlights.note: River and stone country near the Indian border.

highlights.name: Bichnakandi
highlights.note: Limestone river landscape at the foot of the Meghalaya hills.

intro: A northern district with the terracotta masterpiece of Kantajew Temple and the large man-made tank at Ramsagar.
transport: Trains from Dhaka (about 8 hours) and buses.

highlights.name: Kantajew Temple
highlights.note: 18th-century terracotta temple with extraordinary panels.

highlights.name: Ramsagar
highlights.note: Large historic tank with a lakeside park.

highlights.name: Dinajpur Rajbari
highlights.note: Remains of the local royal estate.

intro: A northern river district where the Teesta and Brahmaputra create shifting char land and seasonal flooding.
transport: Buses from Dhaka via Rangpur (about 7 hours).

highlights.name: Teesta Barrage, Dalia
highlights.note: Barrage and river views on the Teesta.

highlights.name: Brahmaputra char land
highlights.note: Seasonal islands and riverbank farming.

tagline: River islands at the top of the delta
intro: One of the most riverine districts in Bangladesh, with chars on the Brahmaputra, Dharla and Teesta.
transport: Buses from Rangpur (about 2 hours).

highlights.name: Chilmari river port
highlights.note: Historic port on the Brahmaputra.

highlights.name: Dharla River
highlights.note: Wide braided river with char settlements.

intro: A northern border district on the Teesta, with tea gardens and the Tin Bigha corridor.
transport: Trains from Dhaka via Rangpur; buses.

highlights.name: Teesta River
highlights.note: River crossings and sandbars.

highlights.name: Tin Bigha corridor
highlights.note: Small border corridor connecting Bangladeshi enclaves.

intro: A northern district with the historic Nilsagar tank, tea estates and the edge of the Chalan Beel.
transport: Trains from Dhaka (about 8 hours) and buses.

highlights.name: Nilsagar
highlights.note: Large 18th-century tank with a Shiva temple.

highlights.name: Tea gardens
highlights.note: Small estates around Saidpur and Nilphamari.

intro: The northernmost district, where tea grows on the plains below the Himalayas and the border meets India at Banglabandha.
transport: Trains from Dhaka (about 9 hours) and buses.

highlights.name: Banglabandha zero point
highlights.note: Northernmost land port on the Indian border.

highlights.name: Teesta riverbank
highlights.note: River and tea-garden landscapes.

intro: The main city of the north-west, with the restored Tajhat Rajbari, Carmichael College and a busy regional market.
transport: Airport; trains and buses from Dhaka (about 7–8 hours).

highlights.name: Tajhat Rajbari
highlights.note: Restored zamindar palace housing a museum.

highlights.name: Carmichael College
highlights.note: Colonial-era campus building.

intro: A mostly agricultural district in the far north-west, with small rivers and mango orchards.
transport: Buses from Rangpur (about 2 hours).

highlights.name: Tangon River
highlights.note: River crossings and farmland.

intro: A district on the Brahmaputra's old channel, long associated with jute and river trade.
transport: Trains and buses from Dhaka (about 4–5 hours).

highlights.name: Brahmaputra riverbank
highlights.note: Wide river views and fishing life.

highlights.name: Jamalpur railway heritage
highlights.note: Colonial-era rail infrastructure on the Dhaka line.

intro: A university city on the Brahmaputra with a colonial-era palace, a riverside promenade and strong folk-culture traditions.
transport: Trains and buses from Dhaka (about 3 hours).

highlights.name: Shashi Lodge
highlights.note: Restored zamindar palace with a museum.

highlights.name: Brahmaputra riverfront
highlights.note: Evening walks along the old channel.

highlights.name: Bangladesh Agricultural University
highlights.note: Green campus and botanical garden.

intro: A district of haors and hills on the Meghalaya border, with the blue water of Birishiri and Susang Durgapur.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 4 hours) and Mymensingh.

highlights.name: Birishiri
highlights.note: Blue-water river and hills near Durgapur.

highlights.name: Susang Durgapur
highlights.note: Garo villages, forest and the Someshwari river.

highlights.name: Durgapur Rajbari
highlights.note: Small palace associated with the local zamindar family.

intro: A district on the northern edge of the Madhupur sal forest, with Garo villages and the Brahmaputra's old channels.
transport: Buses from Dhaka (about 5 hours) and Mymensingh.

highlights.name: Madhupur forest edge
highlights.note: Sal forest and Garo settlements on the district border.

highlights.name: Netai River
highlights.note: Small river with rural ghats.
